title: Dual comparisons and binary scalar-extension tower squares
statement: Let R→S and an invertible R-module sheaf M be on a general site with independent site and coefficient universes and sheafification in the module and internal-Hom universes, and fix binary comparisons e of [lem-sp-scalar-extension-binary-coherence]. There exist normalized internal-dual comparison isomorphisms for all invertible R-modules, contravariantly natural and sending s tensor f to the functional t tensor x ↦ st α(f(x)). For every further map S→T there are binary comparison data after S→T and for R→T, normalized iterated-extension isomorphisms on arbitrary module sheaves sending a tensor (s tensor x) to a β(s) tensor x, and commuting unit and binary tensor tower squares relative to e. The dual comparisons after extension, for the composite, and the tower comparison in the larger internal-Hom universe are normalized by the same evaluation and tensor formulas, and their dual tower square commutes. No powers or power tower squares are asserted.

proof.text: Construct the explicit dual evaluation and naturality from the slice sheafification Hom equivalence. Apply local rank-one invertibility, which determines the inverse of this explicit map uniquely.

Construct the tower forward and reverse maps by multiplying scalars and inserting one. Prove their inverse identities and unit/binary tower squares by tensor descent. Prove the dual tower square as scalarExtensionTowerDual on nested tensor generators and evaluations on every slice. The original item assembles the required comparison data directly from these explicit maps; no additional comparison record or tensor powers are constructed here.
